keyFindings.description: Two texts this change makes false, in two files it rewrote. `docs/kubernetes.md:3715-3717` tells an operator that a pod relaunched onto another node waits for its `ReadWriteOnce` volume to detach from the old one, showing as transient `FailedAttachVolume` or `Multi-Attach` events until the old pod is gone. For an issue pod that is now wrong in both halves: the replacement does not take the predecessor's claim, so there is no detach and no Multi-Attach — what it may wait on is the predecessor's claim being reaped, a different mechanism with different events, which this change's own risk line already records. The paragraph covers issue and controller pods together and the statement still holds for the controller, so it needs the distinction rather than deletion. `scripts/e2e/stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:3566-3567` says the three issue PVCs are 'each selected by the issue label its Sandbox's claim template put on it'; this change removes labels from that claim entirely — the API server prunes them — and the script's own `pod_disk` reads by name and says so, so the comment contradicts the code below it. Both are the stale-prose class this review has filed seven times, and both are in paths this change owns.
keyFindings.note: My thermonuclear quality pass found these and excluded them on a scope rule I gave it — 'do not flag unchanged code'. That instruction was too narrow and the exclusion is mine, not its: what I have meant all along, and filed on seven times, is text a change makes false in a file it owns, not text whose own lines the diff touched. It asked me the question explicitly over IRC and then resolved it against my written boundary, which is the right thing for it to have done with the rule as written.

keyFindings.description: Raised by the tester and routed to me for the judgement: `session_copy`'s stem rule accepts a leading `-`, so `-rf` is a plain name by the character test. It is bounded three ways today — every use is quoted, `mkdir -p --` and `realpath -m --` end their options, and the three stems in use are two literals and a pod name, which DNS-1123 forbids from beginning with `-`. My answer to the architect's question is that it is not worth a round of its own, and that since this round is open for the finding above it should ride in it: one character in the character class. The reason to take it is not today's reachability but that an option-looking name reaching a later consumer is the classic shape of this class, and the whole of this round's fix is about not relying on what a caller happens to pass.

roundSevenVerification.note: The round-7 finding is fixed, and by interface rather than by guard, which is the stronger answer.
verified: session_copy takes PREFIX AREA STEM and no path (:1005-1006). The area keyword resolves to a root inside the function from a three-entry table (:1009-1016), so no caller supplies a destination.

The stem is refused unless it is a plain [A-Za-z0-9._-] name other than . and .. (:1017-1021), and root and destination are both realpath'd with the destination required to be a direct child of the root (:1022-1026) — before the listing, before any derivation and before mkdir (:1027-1029).
All three callers pass literals or a daemon-owned name: `review-pair subagents` (:1171), `transcripts pods` (:2609), `daemon-controller "$pod"` (:5716).
record_pair still computes a stem from the reviewer's recorded session path, but writes it as the contents of review-pair/session-stem rather than as any part of a path (:1175).
The agent-settable values now reach only the SQL key prefix, which selects which rows are read and never where they are written.
